To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

deep learning models trained on different subjects’ views of the same objects show substantial inter-observer differences, and that subjects who create more diverse images of the same object result in models with better object representations.

(1) the first-person data of different subjects contain large inter-observer variability, and (2) the amount of variability is positively correlated with the performance of deep learning object-recognition models.
(1) we can train object-recognition models from first-person images and that (2) these models can be used to gain insight into how different observers perceive objects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the visual system develops in the context of the first-person view.
the question how we can learn more about the human visual system from first-person data using deep learning.
the following question: Can we use deep learning to gain insight into how people perceive objects in first-person videos?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differences between the subjects in this study are large, and that these differences can be captured by deep learning models.

the models trained on the videos from the first-person perspective of each subject are able to learn more robust object recognition models than the models trained on videos from a third-person perspective.
the more diverse the images, the more accurate the models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diversity in a person's visual experience can be used to predict their object-recognition ability.
deep learning models can be used to gain insight into the development of the visual system, and to study the relationship between the visual input and the visual representation.
the diversity of a subject's view is an important factor for the robustness of object recognition models trained on that view.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inter-observer differences in first-person object views can be used to gain insights into the developmental trajectory of the visual system.
the use of deep learning in the context of first-person data can provide a new perspective on human visual development.
the inter-subject differences we observe in our dataset could be a valuable resource for cognitive psychologists and developmental scientists.
